title: Complete two sealed builds back-to-back on fresh worlds
goal: Complete both sealed blueprints - the Stone Arch (idx 0) and the Step Pyramid (idx 1) - as separate judged runs, each on a completely fresh world: compose up, seed, judge, build to block_hit_rate 1.0, score, compose down, then repeat for the second task without reusing any world state. The card verifies the whole campaign, so the minimum of the two recorded block_hit_rate values must be 1.0; a shortcut on either run (stale world, skipped teardown, missing ledger) leaves the campaign RED. Carry lessons from the first run into a written adjustment for the second.
resources: docker image itzg/minecraft-server:2024.6.1-java17 (Minecraft 1.19.2 vanilla; compose file assets/gc-367/docker-compose.yml)
docker image node:20.15.1 (Node 20 runtime for mineflayer bots and the judger's JS bridge)

spec.command: python3 -c "import json;rs=[json.load(open('work/gc-367/MARBLE/marble/result/gc-367-t%d/score.json'%i)) for i in range(2)];print(json.dumps({'min_block_hit_rate':min(float(r['block_hit_rate']) for r in rs)}))"

process_expectations: Two full compose lifecycles (up ... down) appear in the run log, one per task, with no builds started on a leftover world
Separate plan artifacts exist for task 0 and task 1, and the task-1 plan records at least one adjustment learned from task 0
Each run's snapshot verification and mismatch-identity repairs are logged independently under its own task name
Both result ledgers (gc-367-t0, gc-367-t1) were produced by the judger, not hand-written: their end_reason and progression snapshots are consistent with the run log
